rows.grounds: compound; one whose seminal energy flows upward
uncertain reading; possibly instrumental or related to manual action

items.question: What state of being a yogin is attained through this practice, O beloved?
premises: Through this practice one may become ūrdhvaretas.
Such a one is called a yogin.
A mere manual practitioner is not a true yogin.
items.inference: True yogic status here consists in the upward transformation of energy, not in external manual practice alone.
uncertainties: The exact reading and grammatical form of 'karata(?' are unclear.
items.plain_english: O beloved, one may become an upward-flowing yogin; one is not a yogin merely by hand.

items.question: How rare is this circle and is any yoga superior to it?
premises: This circle is hard to obtain.
No yoga exists higher than this.
Its rarity and supremacy are asserted together.
items.inference: The circle is both exceedingly rare and unsurpassed by any other yoga.
items.plain_english: This circle is indeed hard to obtain, and there is no yoga higher than this.

items.question: What result arises when this discipline is practiced step by step?
premises: The practice is undertaken step by step.
Such gradual practice is situated in disciplined repetition.
Its effect is described as causing great wonder.
items.inference: Step-by-step practice of this discipline produces greatly wondrous results.
items.plain_english: When practiced step by step, it indeed produces great wonder.

rows.grounds: locative adverb referring to this matter

items.question: Can there be any doubt about the result for those devoted to constant practice?
premises: Some practitioners are devoted to constant practice.
The verse addresses the outcome in this context.
Doubt about that outcome is explicitly denied.
items.inference: For those devoted to constant practice, the promised result is certain.
items.plain_english: For those devoted to constant practice, there is no doubt here.

items.plain_english: In that, muttering before an image brings about the breaking of pots and stones.

rows.grounds: compound listing deities; sandhi form with final plural marker

items.question: Which great deities are included among the beings encompassed by this vision?
premises: Brahma, Vishnu, Yama, and Indra are named.
Varuna and Vayu are also named.
The list presents major cosmic deities together.
items.inference: The vision encompasses the great deities Brahma, Vishnu, Yama, Indra, Varuna, and Vayu.
items.plain_english: Brahma, Vishnu, Yama, and Indra, and indeed Varuna and Vayu.

items.question: Which other classes of beings are included in this encompassing vision, O beloved?
premises: Gandharvas, Kinnaras, Yakshas, Nagas, and Vidyadharas are named.
These are diverse classes of non-human beings.
They are addressed in continuation of the prior enumeration.
items.inference: The vision also includes Gandharvas, Kinnaras, Yakshas, Nagas, and Vidyadharas.
items.plain_english: O beloved, Gandharvas, Kinnaras, Yakshas, Nagas, and Vidyadharas.

rows.grounds: compound; endowed with constellations and stars
compound; encompassed or formed as the cosmic egg

items.question: What cosmic totality is presented as endowed with stars and encompassed as a universe?
premises: The object is described as endowed with constellations and stars.
The same object is described as the encompassed cosmic egg.
Both descriptions qualify a single cosmic totality.
items.inference: The verse presents the star-filled cosmic egg as a single encompassed totality.
items.plain_english: The universe, endowed with constellations and stars and encompassed as the cosmic egg.

items.question: What can constant meditation enable one to reveal about one's own body?
premises: Constant meditation is the stated cause.
One's own body is the object shown.
The showing occurs in many ways.
items.inference: Through constant meditation, one may reveal one's own body in manifold ways.
items.plain_english: Through constant meditation, one may show one's own body in many ways.

items.question: What kind of accomplishment does sustained practice bestow according to scripture?
premises: Practice is the cause of the result.
The result bestowed is accomplishment.
This accomplishment is eightfold and enjoined by scripture.
items.inference: Sustained practice bestows the eightfold accomplishment prescribed by scripture.
items.plain_english: From practice, accomplishment gives itself eightfold, as enjoined by scripture.

items.question: To whom may this Kaula teaching be given and to whom must it be withheld?
premises: This Kaula teaching is to be given to the worthy.
It is explicitly not to be given to just anyone.
The verse sets a rule of restricted transmission.
items.inference: This Kaula teaching must be transmitted only to the worthy and withheld from all others.
items.plain_english: This Kaula teaching should be given to the worthy; it should not be given to just anyone.

rows.grounds: compound; this extracted teaching or essence

items.question: How must one who is firmly resolved treat this extracted teaching?
premises: This extracted teaching is the object of instruction.
It is declared to be always concealed.
The instruction is directed to one who is firmly resolved.
items.inference: One who is firmly resolved must always keep this extracted teaching secret.
items.plain_english: This extraction is indeed to be kept secret always by one who is firmly resolved.
